cases.purpose: Verify process-group SIGINT interrupts both default and trapped sleep promptly, preserves the sibling group, and reports the external sleep status to the trap-following script.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 sleep(1) driven by the identical GNU Bash 5.3.15 job-control script
cases.comparison: The historical process-group fixture with an explicit trapped sleep status assertion and a four-second upper bound; compare both candidate and GNU reference outputs and exit status. Readiness and group isolation remain as in migration-sleep-sigint-group-r2.
cases.script:
exec 2>>"$HOME/shell-stderr.log"
set -m
exec 9<>pace.fifo
pause() { read -r -t 0.02 -u 9 _; return 0; }
stat_fields() { local line; read -r line <"/proc/$1/stat" 2>/dev/null || return 1; printf '%s' "${line##*) }"; }
member_sleeping() {
  local f pid w a
  for f in /proc/[0-9]*/stat; do
    pid=${f#/proc/}; pid=${pid%/stat}
    a=($(stat_fields "$pid")) || continue
    [[ ${a[2]} == "$1" && ${a[0]} == S ]] || continue
    w=$(<"/proc/$pid/wchan") 2>/dev/null || continue
    [[ $w == *sleep* || $w == *select* || $w == *poll* || $w == *hrtimer* ]] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}
await() { local i; for ((i = 0; i < 250; i++)); do member_sleeping "$1" && return 0; pause; done; return 1; }
own_group() { local a; a=($(stat_fields "$1")); [[ ${a[2]} == "$1" ]]; }
printf '[default-int]\n'
sleep 20 &
sib=$!
await "$sib" && printf 'sibling-ready\n' || printf 'sibling-not-ready\n'
sleep 20 &
target=$!
await "$target" && printf 'target-ready\n' || printf 'target-not-ready\n'
own_group "$target" && own_group "$sib" && [[ $target != "$sib" ]] && printf 'separate-groups=yes\n' || printf 'separate-groups=no\n'
builtin kill -INT -- "-$target"
wait "$target"
printf 'target-status=%d\n' "$?"
member_sleeping "$sib" && printf 'sibling-unaffected\n' || printf 'sibling-disturbed\n'
builtin kill -TERM -- "-$sib"
wait "$sib"
printf 'sibling-status=%d\n' "$?"
printf '[trapped]\n'
( trap 'printf "trap-ran\n"' INT; start=${EPOCHREALTIME/./}; sleep 10; rc=$?; end=${EPOCHREALTIME/./}; printf 'sleep-returned=%d\n' "$rc"; (( rc == 130 && 10#$end - 10#$start < 4000000 )) || exit 99; exit 7 ) &
target=$!
await "$target" && printf 'target-ready\n' || printf 'target-not-ready\n'
builtin kill -INT -- "-$target"
wait "$target"
rc=$?
printf 'target-status=%d\n' "$rc"
(( rc == 7 )) || exit 1
printf 'done\n'
